idiom_name: Vapor req.auth (authenticator + guard middleware); @TaskLocal for code outside the request chain
implementation_notes: In the dominant Swift server framework the container is the request: an Authenticator verifies once and populates req.auth, guards call req.auth.require(User.self), and User.guardMiddleware() adds the requirement separately so authenticators stay composable. For code that runs without a Vapor request - Swift-native services, background work started from a request - the concurrency mechanism is @TaskLocal, which binds a value for the dynamic extent of a task and implicitly carries it to child tasks (TaskGroup, async let) while Task.detached does not inherit it. The classic context object is unnecessary in Vapor; a hand-written TaskLocal-bound context is justified when a guard sits outside the request chain, and it should hold an immutable Sendable value.
pitfalls: req.auth is per-request: helpers that receive only the user value lose the security context, so pass the request (or the principal) explicitly instead of reaching for a global.
Task.detached does not inherit task-local values while Task { } copies them - a detached child reading the principal sees the default (often nil), so bind explicitly or avoid detaching.
Binding a task-local outside any task falls back to a thread-local binding for the duration of withValue, which works in synchronous code but does not travel to other threads.
